body: claimed: main session (agent: biarc fit for morph spirals) · 2026-11-07T03:56Z · worktree on dd8bc95 · plan: a tangent-constrained biarc fit so the morph-spiral chords the kink law refuses as single arcs become proved arc pairs; moves count down, kink/area/crossing proofs kept.

agent a314c53d (worktree agent-a314c53d4fbf6195b), time box spent. **Nothing is staged.** The patch is left unstaged in the worktree for review.

**What was built.** `machining2d/arc_biarc.rs` is the second attempt for an arc the kink proof refuses. It fits an equal-leg biarc (Bolton 1975; arc splines per Meek & Walton) between the run's ends. Each end tangent is the plan's own: the bisector of its unit chords (a centred difference). If a run does not hold, it is halved at its middle vertex, down to 3 chords. Each biarc must pass:
- the two-way 0.25 x tol hug
- a curvature reading: its heading stays inside the cone of the plan's chords at every vertex and chord middle, and no plan vertex in the run turns more than 5 deg
- the area bracket (`proved`)
- the kink law on the arcs' true tangents (`kink_free`)
- a checked tangent-continuous joint

`judge` now treats a biarc (whose joint is not a pass vertex) as one unit, and the crossing law refuses it as one unit.

| rectangle | 18372 -> 12502 | 888 -> 4116 | 665 -> 221 |
| L-pocket | 51788 -> 33778 | 2642 -> 13630 | 1972 -> 482 |

0 breaks past 5 deg on every fixture, and the verifier is silent.

**Blocker.** `hsm_report_full_resolution` fails: the L-pocket reads 16.7 % D, over the 14.6 % + 10 % law. Before the change it read 15.4 %. The peak is at (20.67, 27.26), the spiral's tight start. There, a nearly straight arc with R 45 mm (posted move 734, (20.7191, 27.1920) -> (20.6683, 27.2623)) sits next to arcs of R 0.4 mm. The corner guard and the cone check did not remove it, so it may not be a biarc piece at all. That has not been traced yet.

**Not run** because of the blocker: `-Tier quick`, app `golden_cl` / `operations`, clippy.

**Next step.** Find out which fit produces move 734 and why the load reader reads +2 deg there: does the reader's heading under the 5 deg break fallback treat that spot differently on chords and on arcs?

Round 2 (worktree agent-a43a4cfd21d2bf330): **the cause is in the geometry, not in the load reader**. The patch is staged and not committed.

**Trace.** Posted moves 734 + 735 are one biarc over plan vertices 5248..5252 (a half of the run 5248..5256). It pairs a CW arc of R 45.2 with a CCW arc of R 0.43, and the joint (20.6683, 27.2623) sits 6 um from plan vertex 5249, at the load peak. On those four chords the plan turns about 11 deg (vertex bends 2.8 / 3.8 / 3.5 deg). The biarc puts that whole turn into the R 0.43 arc and runs the R 45 arc straight before it. So the arc's true tangent at the joint is 125.76 deg, while the plan's centred tangent there is 126.6 deg: 0.85 deg behind, toward the stock. The cone check `follows` allows that (0.48 / 2.24 deg against a 2.8 deg bend). The joint's ~6 um offset from the chords changes the load by <0.1 deg, so position is not the cause; the heading is.

**The reader is right.** Its window edge sits at the true perpendicular, so heading into the stock really does read more engagement. As an A/B, I posted the same biarc path as chords with the #10 bisector heading: it read 48.5 deg / 16.04 % at the same point. The bisector at a curvature jump splits the two chords, so it hides about half of the lag. The arc reading of 49.5 deg / 16.7 % is the honest one.

**Fix.** `RATIO = 4`: the two radii of a biarc must stay within 4x of each other, so the run stays chords or halves further. This is pinned by `a_biarc_bunching_the_turn_into_one_arc_is_refused` (the plan's real vertices; it fails without the limit). I also fixed the round-1 unit test's biarc data (it posed a straight leg, so `biarc` correctly returned None). It now uses a quarter circle.
